subject: 3-level model with temporal autocorrelation at one level

messages.author: ca74381630759742
messages.subject: 3-level model with temporal autocorrelation at one level
parts:
Greetings list,

My data are annual measures of employees, and employees are nested within office locations. This can be thought of time (level 1) nested within employees (level 2), who are nested within offices (level 3). 

I would like to specify a model with the repeated measures per employee with a random intercept that handles temporal autocorrelation (ar1 or rw1), and then have random intercepts for the offices. (The offices do not have spatial autcorrelation to worry about.)

How do I specify that?

mod1 <- inla(outcome ~ main_predictor + covariate + covariate_2 + ... + 
                    f(employee_id, model = 'ar2') + 
                    f(office_id, model = 'iid'))

But how does the inla know that employees are nested within office locations? mod1 would have two random effects, one for employees and one for offices. I would like the three-level hierarchy to be explicit.

Would this work?

mod2 <- inla(outcome ~ main_predictor + covariate + covariate_2 + ... +
                    f(employee_id, group = office_id, model = list('ar2', 'iid')))

or maybe?

mod3 <- inla(outcome ~ main_predictor + covariate + covariate_2 + ... +
                    f(office_id, model = 'iid',  group = employee_id, control.group = list(model = 'ar1'))

Any resources on three-level models, and information on repeated measures with temporal autocorrelation nested within another level in particular would be most appreciated. 

Apologies if this information is readily available. I could not find it. 

Thanks for great software, 
Dexter

parts:
f(, model="iid", group=..., control.group=list(model='ar1'))

is the same as

f(, model="ar1", replicate = r)


replicated measurements, for index 1, say, is just to let index 1 appear
more than once, like

idx = c(1,1,1, 2)

f(idx, ...)

which say that index 1 is measured three times, with y[1:3]

maybe easier to respond, if you simulate data that do what you want.
then I can see exactly what you're aiming at.

Thank you. Apologies: this reprex is not a succinct as is possible.. but I hope it conveys the overall set up.

library(tidyverse)
library(INLA)

set.seed(19870630) # wife's birthday, for reproducibility

# employee membership in office locations, uneven clusters at office level (in reality there are ~700 offices, not 6 )
employee_locs <- tribble(
  ~'employee_id', ~'office',
  'A', 'New York',
  'B', 'New York',
  'C', 'Mexico City',
  'D', 'Toronto',
  'E', 'London',
  'F', 'Stockholm',
  'G', 'New York',
  'H', 'London',
  'I', 'Tokyo',
  'J',  'London',
  'K', 'Stockholm',
  'L', 'Stockholm',
  'M', 'London',
  'N', 'Tokyo',
  'O', 'London',
  'P', 'Tokyo',
  'Q', 'London',
  'R', 'Mexico City',
  'S', 'London',
  'T', 'Toronto',
  'U', 'Mexico City',
  'V', 'Stockholm',
  'W', 'Stockholm',
  'X', 'Tokyo',
  'Y', 'London',
  'Z', 'Mexico City'
)

# cluster size at office level is imbalanced
table(employee_locs$office)

# make fake data of employees starting between years 1969 to 1999, with different overall duration
dat <-
  tibble(employee_id = sort(sample(LETTERS, 1000, replace = TRUE))) |>
  group_by(employee_id) |>
  mutate(n_years = n(),
         first_year = sample(1969:1999, 1),
         last_year = first_year + n_years
         ) |>
  ungroup() |> # surely there is a more straightforward way to simulate this structure, sorry.
  distinct() |>
  group_by() |>
  mutate(year = list(tibble(years = NA_integer_))) |>
  group_by(employee_id) |>
  mutate(year = map(year, ~seq(first_year, last_year))) |>
  unnest(year) |>
  ungroup() %>%
  # some random y outcome
  mutate(y = rnorm(nrow(.)),        # in reality it has serial autocorrelation per employee_id from year to year
         x1 = rnorm(nrow(.), 10),    # an employee-year level predictor
         x2 = rnorm(nrow(.), 50, 2) # another plausible predictor at the employee-year level
         ) |>
  left_join(employee_locs, by = 'employee_id') |> # add in office locations, to be random effects
  select(y, x1, x2, employee_id, year, office)    # clean up and reorder columns

dat

# visualize data
dat |>
  ggplot(aes(year, y, group = employee_id, color = employee_id)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~office)

# repeated measures of employees, employees within distinct offices.

# doesn't actually run
mod <- inla(y ~ x1 + x2 +
              f(employee_id, model = 'ar1', group = office, control.group = list(model = 'iid')),
            data = dat
            )

summary(mod)

is this a specification that allows for an ar1 serial autocorrelation of intercepts for the employees (autocorrelation by time), while having employees nested within locations (addressing non-independence of offices via random intercepts)?

Thank you, Dexter

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] 3-level model with temporal autocorrelation at one level
parts:
It occurred to me that simpler set up would be to use the sleepstudy data in lme4. 

My intention is to articulate the questions better here. 

library(tidyverse)
library(INLA)
library(lme4) # has sleepstudy data

data(sleepstudy)

# create a fake grouping of subjects
look_up <-
  tribble(
    ~'Subject', ~'Group',
    308, 'A',
    309, 'B',
    310, 'A',
    330, 'C',
    331, 'C',
    332, 'A',
    333, 'B',
    334, 'E',
    335, 'D',
    337, 'E',
    349, 'C',
    350, 'B',
    351, 'E',
    352, 'B',
    369, 'D',
    370, 'D',
    371, 'A',
    372, 'B') |>
  mutate(Subject = as.factor(Subject))

# add third-level group
(dat <- sleepstudy |> as_tibble() |> left_join(look_up, by = 'Subject'))

table(dat$Group)

# visualize set up
dat |>
  ggplot(aes(Days, Reaction)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm', se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(Group~Subject) +
  NULL

# frequentist model
mod_lmer   <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), data = dat)

# bayesian analogue with inla
mod_iid    <- inla(Reaction ~ Days + f(Subject, model = 'iid'), data = dat)

# similar estimates for both, successful double check
summary(mod_lmer)
mod_iid$summary.fixed

# suppose the data had a stronger temporal autocorrelation component, we could use
mod_ar1        <- inla(Reaction ~ Days + f(Subject, model = 'ar1'), data = dat) # or
mod_rw1        <- inla(Reaction ~ Days + f(Subject, model = 'rw1'), data = dat)

# instead of 'iid', great.

# but employees are now nested in Groups. The frequentist model could be
mod_lmer_3 <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Group/Subject), data = dat)

# but lacks the desired correlation structure at the Subject level (like mod_ar1 and mod_rw1 above).
# Note that lmer complains about singularity

# Question 1: what is the inla equivalent? Something else?
mod_3a      <- inla(Reaction ~ Days + f(Subject, group = Group, model = 'iid'))
mod_3b      <- inla(Reaction ~ Days + f(Group, replicate = Subject, model = 'iid'))

# neither run.

# Question 2: how can that be extended to have ar1 within subjects and iid within groups?
mod_3_ar1_g  <- inla(Reaction ~ Days + f(Subject
                                       , model = 'iid'
                                       , group = Group
                                       , control.group = list(model = 'ar1'))
                   , data = dat)

mod_3_ar1_r  <- inla(Reaction ~ Days + f(Group
                                       , model = 'ar1'
                                       , replicate = Subject
                                       )
                   , data = dat)

# end

Thank you for your consideration,
Dexter
